items.title: The Acoustic Science of What Makes a Great Singer
items.snippet: What separates a good opera singer from a great one in the ears of competition judges? Keio University researchers simulated a live vocal competition, revealing that the 2–4 kHz "singer’s formant" and sex-specific vibrato tuning drive top marks, while raw loudness matters little.

items.title: How Octopuses Lock in Long-Term Memory Without New Proteins
items.snippet: How does an octopus hold onto memories without the molecular machinery used by humans? Researchers discovered a self-sustaining nitric oxide switch in the octopus vertical lobe that locks in long-term potentiation without requiring new protein synthesis.

items.title: Enriched Environments Rewire the Brain via Shared Synaptic Gene Networks
items.snippet: How does an active, stimulating lifestyle physically rewire the brain? A meta-analysis of over 300 studies identifies a conserved molecular signature driven by the AP-1 transcription factor, unveiling the genomic machinery behind environmental enrichment.

items.title: Scientists discover mysterious “lonely” brain waves linked to memory loss
items.snippet: Scientists have uncovered a surprising link between Alzheimer’s-related protein buildup, disrupted brain waves during deep sleep, and fading memory. The findings suggest that hidden changes in how the brain processes memories overnight may contribute to age-related memory loss long before Alzheimer’s symptoms appear.
